updated aviation discussion

.SYNOPSIS...25/1156 PM.

Warm temperatures and dry weather is expected through Saturday due
to a predominant offshore flow pattern. Temperatures will peak on
today and Friday with some gusty northeast winds at times, then 
cooling will begin over the weekend. There is an increasing 
possibility of a large storm system around the middle of next 
week.

&&

.SHORT TERM (TDY-SAT)...26/850 AM.

***UPDATE***

Very little impactful weather in the short term. Some locally
gusty Santa Ana winds this morning and again tomorrow morning.
Temperatures will be 10-15 degrees above normal through Friday
before a cooling trend begins Saturday. Next chance of rain is
Sunday afternoon into Monday morning but just very light amounts 
expected and possibly little to no measurable in some areas.

***From Previous Discussion***

Three very warm days on tap for Srn CA. A large upper high to the
SW will keep a ridge in place over the area through the period.
Hgts will climb to 588 dam today, remain there Friday and then
slowly fall to 582 dam on Saturday. More importantly sfc high
pressure to the N and NE will bring 60 hours of offshore flow to 
the area. The offshore flow will peak today at around 6 mb from 
both the N and E. There is not much upper support, but the 
gradients alone should be about to bring low end advisory gusts to
the Santa Lucias, Santa Susanas and western San Gabriels. Other 
wind prone areas will have winds that will be just below advisory 
levels. The winds will subside a little on Friday and will be
noticeably weaker on Saturday.

Skies will be mostly clear and at worst partly cloudy if some high
clouds struggle through the ridge.

Temperatures will be the main talking point of the short term. The
usual combination of sunshine, higher than normal hgts and
offshore flow will all combine to bring above normal temps all
three days. Highs today will be in the upper 70s to mid 80s across
the csts/vly south of Pt Conception with mid 70s to lower 80s
north. 1 to 3 degrees of additional warming will make Friday the
warmest day with max temps 12 to 15 degrees above normal. Lowering
hgts and weaker offshore flow (and a possible return to onshore
flow in the afternoon) will bring 4 to 8 degrees of cooling to the
area Saturday with highs still remaining above normal.

.LONG TERM (SUN-WED)...26/1227 AM.

The storm door will open slowly on Sunday as the tail end of a far
northern storm system drifts over the area. Look for chc of rain
across the Central Coast in the afternoon with rain becoming
likely there in the evening. The rest of the area will be dry with
increasing clouds and 3 to 6 degree cooling trend.

light rain will continue overnight across the Central Coast, while
a 20 to 30 percent chc of light rain develops south of Pt
Conception. Rain totals Sunday and overnight will be less than a
quarter inch and more likely under a tenth and only across the
Central Coast.

On Monday, Sunday's storm will be to the east of the area but 
moist slightly difluent flow ahead of the next storm will
overspread the area. The day will be cloudy with a 30 to 40
percent chc of rain morning, afternoon and evening. A quarter to a
third of inch of rain my fall during this time highest across the
coastal slopes and Central Coast. 2 to 4 degrees of cooling will
bring max temps to near normal values.

There is remarkable agreement between all deterministic, AI and
ensemble based forecasts that there will be a moderate to strong
storm moving over the area Tue/Wed. A cold upper low is forecast
to dive to the SSE and move over Srn CA sometime Tuesday or
Tuesday night. The current forecast shows the heaviest rain
falling Tuesday and then tapering off Wednesday, but the timing
could easily change by 12 or so hours as the day draws nearer.
This looks like it will be moderate system bring 1 to 3 inches of
rain to the csts and vlys with 3 to 5 inches across the coast
facing slopes and .5 to 1.5 inches across the far interior
sections. If the upper low does pass overhead there will be chc of
TSTMs as well. Snow will not much of a concern with accumulations
likely only at 7500+ ft. Max temps will mostly be in the 60s both
days.

&&

.AVIATION...26/1745Z.

At 17Z at KLAX, there was a surface-based inversion. The top of
the inversion was at 3300 feet with a temp of 22 deg C.

High confidence in all TAFs with VFR conds expected thru the fcst
period.

KLAX...High confidence in VFR TAF. Good confidence that any east 
wind component remains below 7 kts. N to NE winds around 5 kt are 
possible thru 26/20Z and again 27/05Z-20Z.

KBUR...High confidence in VFR TAF.

&&

.MARINE...26/842 AM.

For the Outer Waters, moderate to high confidence in current 
forecast. Expecting Small Craft Advisory (SCA) level seas with 
areas of SCA level winds to persist through Friday night. Then 
conds will be largely below SCA levels Saturday through Monday 
before winds increase Monday night to SCA levels or higher ahead 
of an approaching strong storm system.

For the Inner Waters north of Point Sal, moderate to high 
confidence in current forecast. Expecting SCA level seas lasting 
through Friday night. E to NE SCA level winds are expected at 
times through Friday morning. Winds increase again Monday night to
SCA levels or higher ahead of an approaching strong storm system.

For the Inner Waters south of Point Conception, moderate to high
confidence in current forecast. Through tonight, winds will 
generally be below SCA levels, except for the near shore waters 
from Point Mugu to Santa Monica where offshore SCA level winds 
are expected through this afternoon. For Friday through Monday, 
winds and seas are expected to remain below SCA. Winds are 
expected to increase to SCA levels Monday night ahead of an 
approaching strong storm system.

A large, west long period swell will create hazardous boating
conditions through today for the coastal waters, by creating 
large breaking waves near coastlines and possibly also near harbor
entrances. These waves can capsize small vessels. Follow guidance
from local officials.

&&

.BEACHES...26/844 AM.

A large, long period, west swell will persist today over the 
coastal waters. This large swell will combine with exceptionally 
high tides to bring large surf to the area as well as moderate to 
significant coastal flooding. Much above normal tides will
continue into Friday morning as well.

The highest surf and most significant coastal flooding issues are
expected across the Central Coast from Point Conception northward, as
well as the Ventura County coastline, and far eastern portions of
the southern Santa Barbara County coasts through this morning. 
Elsewhere, the surf and coastal flooding issues are a bit less, 
but still concerning. The morning high tide will be the timing of 
greatest concern for coastal flooding, and low lying coastal areas
with no protection from the ocean will be more vulnerable. 
Coastal structures are at an increased risk for damage. There will
be many, strong rip currently nearly everywhere, strong long 
shore currents, a risk of sneaker waves, large shore pound, 
coastal erosion. These conditions will lead to an increased risk 
of drowning and make swimming dangerous.

Please check out LAXCFWLOX for the latest details about all of the
current advisories and warnings in effect.
